title: Cancel a subscription (UK)
summary: UK variant: cancel a distance-contract subscription, citing the 14-day cancellation right and the UK's strengthened subscription rules.
goal_default: Please cancel my subscription, stop all future billing, and confirm in writing with an effective date.

rights.claim: For a distance contract, you generally have a 14-day right to cancel from the day it was entered into.
rights.basis: The Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013.

rights.claim: UK law is strengthening subscription rules — clearer information, cancellation reminders, and an easy exit.
rights.basis: Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 (subscription contracts provisions).

rights.claim: If you are billed after a confirmed cancellation, your card issuer can reverse it via chargeback.
rights.basis: Card-scheme chargeback rules; Section 75 protection may also apply for credit-card purchases.

ladder: In-app / written cancellation to the provider
Card-issuer chargeback if billed after cancellation
Trading Standards / Citizens Advice consumer service

artifact.subject: Cancellation of my subscription{{account_suffix}} — written notice (UK)
artifact.body:
To: {{target}} Billing / Support

Hello,

I am writing to cancel my subscription{{account_suffix}}. {{goal}}

Please treat this as formal written notice. Where a 14-day cancellation right under the Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013 applies, I am exercising it. If any charge is taken after this notice, I will ask my card issuer to reverse it.

Please reply within 5 business days with written confirmation and the effective date.

Sincerely,
{{name}}

disclaimer: This is information about your rights, not legal advice, and guarantees no outcome. Whether the 14-day right applies depends on the contract and timing.
